about.title: Rio Dell Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Rio Dell is a small Humboldt County community, and many residents rely on nearby clinics and regional hospitals for care. When something goes wrong during treatment, patients and families are often left with more questions than answers. Was it simply an unfortunate outcome, or did a provider fall short of the standard of care? California law sets a narrow window to act and requires input from a qualified medical expert before a malpractice claim can move forward. Our team reviews medical records, evaluates whether a provider's actions met accepted standards, and explains your options honestly. We offer a free consultation, and we work on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless your case results in a recovery. If you or a loved one suspect a medical error caused harm, it's worth having someone knowledgeable take a look at the facts.

items.title: Time Limits Are Strict
items.desc: California generally requires malpractice claims to be filed within one year of discovering the harm, and no later than three years from the injury itself. A 90-day pre-suit notice is also typically required before a lawsuit can be filed.

items.title: Expert Review Matters
items.desc: California law almost always requires a qualified medical expert to support a malpractice claim. Our team can help arrange that review so your situation is evaluated properly.

items.title: Non-Economic Damages Are Capped, But Rising
items.desc: California's MICRA cap on non-economic damages increases annually, and understanding how that applies to your specific circumstances is something we can walk you through.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after a procedure near Rio Dell. Does that automatically mean malpractice occurred?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law recognizes that medicine involves risk, and a poor result alone doesn't establish negligence. We would need to review whether the provider's actions fell below the accepted standard of care.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim if I live in Rio Dell?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you one year from when you discover the harm, but no more than three years from when the injury occurred. There's also a required 90-day notice period before filing suit, so it's best not to wait too long to have your situation reviewed.

items.question: Do I need to travel outside Rio Dell to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Our team handles consultations remotely or can arrange to meet you closer to home in Humboldt County. We're here to make the process as convenient as possible.
